messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am trying to use the Cardinal package to read MSI data and face a few problem so I would like to know if I am doing it right.
I used previously the readmzxml package to read MS data and output is quite different.

Here is my code:

library(maggritr)
library(Cardinal)

## Set some options
mass.accuracy = 0.025
resolution_redim = 3
Int_threshold = 2000
initial_dim = 30

## Read the data file: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs00216-014-8357-8
data = Cardinal::readImzML("HR2MSI mouse urinary bladder S096",
                           mass.accuracy = mass.accuracy,units.accuracy = "mz")

## extract the dense matrix
data2 = imageData(data)[features(data),seq(from=1,to=260,by=resolution_redim),seq(from=1,to=134,by=resolution_redim)]
# print(dim(data2))
# print(sum(apply(data2,1,max)>Int_threshold))

## apply the threshold
data2 = data2[which(apply(data2,1,max)>Int_threshold),,]

# the rest is my analysis, I put it so you understand what I am doing
## flatten the array (DLC package on github: https://github.com/DimitriF/DLC), this lead to a matrix with one row per masses and one column per pixel
decon  = DLC::deconstruct(truc,margin=1,transform=T)

## normalization and first dimension reduction
model = decon %>%
  prospectr::standardNormalVariate() %>%
  ChemometricsWithR::PCA()
data3 = model$scores[,1:initial_dim]

## second dimension reduction with tsne
set.seed(1)
model2 = Rtsne(mat,dims = 2,perplexity = 5,max_iter = 1000,verbose = F,pca = F)

## plot the tsne map, similar images clusterize together
plot(model2$Y,pch=".")

And my questions:

- The data is in profile format and not centroid as I am used to, is there a way to make the peak peaking before the bining ?
- Is there a "apply like" function to apply the intensity threshold filtering before extracting the dense array ? I need to remove low intensity masses later anyway.
- For the analysis, do you have something similar ?

The documentation was quite extensive and there are lots of functions in this package so I apologize if the answer was already present.

Regards
Dimitri

messages.body_plain:
Hi Dimitri,

1. Yes, the walkthrough vignette as well as the workflow vignettes from the CardinalWorkflows have examples of peak picking and binning.

http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/data/experiment/vignettes/CardinalWorkflows/inst/doc/Workflows-clustering.pdf
http://bioconductor.org/packages/release/data/experiment/vignettes/CardinalWorkflows/inst/doc/Workflows-classification.pdf

2. There are pixelApply() and featureApply() functions, yes. These will work on the pixels or mass features, respectively.

3. There is a Cardinal::PCA() function for performing PCA; t-SNE is not currently implemented natively.

It looks like you are going through extra trouble to change the data from datacube into matrix format where rows are features and columns are pixels. This is how the data is internally stored and can be accessed via the iData() accessor . (There is also a spectra() accessor alias for it.)

-Kylie

messages.subject: Assigning sample names to pixels
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I have measured a tissue microarray which contains many tissue samples and each sample has regions with diseased and healthy tissue.
This means I need to assign a sample name as well as a diagnosis to each pixel.
The assignment of the diagnosis worked well as elsewhere proposed in this forum:

normal <- select(msidata, mz=150)
diseased<- select(msidata, mz=150)
diagnosis <- as.character(rep(NA, ncol(msidata)))
diagnosis[normal] <- "normal"
diagnosis[diseased] <- "diseased"
diagnosis <- as.factor(diagnosis)
msidata$diagnosis = diagnosis

But I found no satisfying way to do the same for sample names, I tried
sample1 <- select(msidata, mz=150)
sample2 <- select(msidata, mz=150)
sample_names <- as.character(rep(NA, ncol(msidata)))
sample_names[sample1] <- "sample1"
sample_names[sample2] <- "sample2"
sample_names <- as.factor(sample_names)
msidata$sample = sample_names

This looks ok on first glance, but does not work with PLS, PCA,...

sampleNames(msidata)
[1] "sample1" "sample2"

validObject(msidata)
Error in validObject(msidata) :
  invalid class “MSImageSet” object: sample names differ between pixelData and protocolData

test = PLS(msidata,y=msidata$diagnosis, ncomp=2)
PLS: Centering data.
PLS: Fitting partial least squares components.
Error in `sampleNames<-`(`*tmp*`, value = c("sample1", "sample2")) :
  number of new names (2) should equal number of rows in AnnotatedDataFrame (1)

Does anyone know how to correctly assign sample names within one MSI datafile?

Thanks in advance,
Melanie

messages.subject: Re: Assigning sample names to pixels
messages.body_plain:
The $sample column and sampleNames() method are special, and they actually correspond to the slide/run. You are saying these observations come from separate slides / separate runs. If that's what you intend to do, then it's a little convoluted, but you do something like this:

varMetadata(msidata)["sample","labelType"] <- "dim"

protocolData(msidata) <- AnnotatedDataFrame(
data=data.frame(row.names=sampleNames(msidata)))

msidata <- regeneratePositions(msidata)

If that's not what you mean to do, then choose a different name for the column besides "sample", which is treated specially and particular expectations for it.

-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: Select Command
messages.body_plain:
Hey Jack,

the select function does not give you a new image subset but only the information if the pixel is in your ROI or not (logical vector with TRUE and FALSE for each pixel). You need a second step in which you filter your imaging data for the pixels which are TRUE (within your ROI):

ROI_pixels = select(msidata, mode="region", colorkey=FALSE) #select ROI
ROI_image = msidata[,ROI_pixels] # subset original dataset for ROI
image(ROI_image, mz=1) # visual control

Best,
Melanie
